message.content:
Buddhism was founded by **Siddhartha Gautama**, who is commonly referred to as the **Buddha** (“the awakened one”).  
He was born in the 6th–5th century BCE in the area that is today **Lumbini, Nepal** (then part of ancient India). After attaining enlightenment under the Bodhi tree at **Bodh Gaya in present‑day Bihar, India**, he began teaching his insights, which later became the foundation of Buddhism. Thus, Buddhism originated in the **Indian subcontinent**—specifically in the region that now spans parts of modern Nepal and northern India.

He was born in Lumbini, in present-day Nepal, around 563 BCE. He attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, in present-day Bihar, India. So the founder is Siddhartha Gautama, also known as the Buddha. Origin: Ancient India, specifically the Indian subcontinent, in the region of modern-day Nepal and India.
